name: Twilight Tome
description: Twilight Tome is tidally locked to its red dwarf parent star, creating a world divided into three distinct zones: a sun-scorched dayside, a frozen nightside, and a habitable twilight band that rings the planet like the spine of an open book. Along this terminator zone, geothermal vents warm the soil and perpetual storm systems churn where hot and cold air masses collide. The twilight sky is a permanent gradient from deep crimson to star-flecked black.

Life in the habitable band exists in a state of eternal dusk. Bioluminescent organisms have evolved to supplement the dim red light, and the forests glow with soft phosphorescence that shifts in response to atmospheric pressure changes. The fauna—mostly low-slung, heavily furred creatures—navigate by a combination of echolocation and light-sensing organs that can detect the faintest bioluminescent signatures across kilometers.

An automated navigation beacon was placed here by an early survey mission, marking Twilight Tome as a safe harbor along a minor trade route. Over time the beacon has become a waypoint for independent pilots and small freighters avoiding the more regulated shipping lanes. The planet's unusual tidal lock has made it a subject of interest for climatologists studying atmospheric dynamics in extreme conditions.

The twilight band's ecosystem is remarkably self-contained, but recent surveys suggest the habitable zone is narrowing as the planet's orbital characteristics shift imperceptibly over millennia. The storm systems along the terminator have intensified in the past century, and some biologists warn that the unique fauna adapted to this razor-thin habitable strip may face extinction within a few thousand years. For now, Twilight Tome remains a living text on the fragility of habitability.
